help.usage:
%1 %2 — Google Drive on Omarchy, mounted by rclone + systemd.

Usage: %1 <command> [options]

Commands:
  setup      Guided, idempotent install. Adopts a mount you made by hand.
             --client            only add/replace your own OAuth client
             --credentials FILE  use this client_secret_*.json
             --shared-client     keep rclone's shared client (not recommended)
             --adopt | --replace what to do with an existing unit
             --remote NAME       rclone remote name (default: gdrive)
             --mountpoint DIR    where to mount (default: ~/GoogleDrive)
             --service NAME      systemd user unit name (default: rclone-gdrive)
  status     Current state (add --json for machines)
  start | stop | restart
  logs       Follow the service log (-n N, --no-follow)
  doctor     Check tools, credentials, network, service, mount and cache (--fix)
  quota      Drive usage (--json)
  open       Open the mount in your file manager
  remove     Undo everything on this machine (--keep-remote, --purge-cache)

Global: --yes  --json  --quiet  --version  --help
err.noUnit: No service installed yet. Run: %1 setup
deps.missingNoPacman: Missing: %1 — install them with your package manager and run setup again.
status.stopped: Not mounted (%1). Start it with: omarchy-gdrive start
status.error: Mount problem at %1 — run: omarchy-gdrive doctor
status.unconfigured: Not set up yet. Run: %1 setup
start.timeout: The service started but nothing is mounted yet. Last log lines:
stop.pending: %1 file(s) are still waiting to be uploaded. Stopping now keeps them in the local cache until the next start.
open.notMounted: Drive is not mounted right now; opening the empty folder.
quota.unavailable: Could not read the quota (offline, or token problem).
doctor.title: %1 — doctor
doctor.noRclone: rclone is not installed (sudo pacman -S rclone)
doctor.confPermsBad: %1 has mode %2 — it holds your token. Fix with: %3 doctor --fix
doctor.noRemote: Remote '%1' not found in rclone. Run: %2 setup
doctor.token: Token valid — Drive answered a listing
doctor.tokenBad: Drive did not answer. Token expired or revoked? Try: rclone config reconnect %1:
doctor.vfsFull: --vfs-cache-mode full (safe for editing files in place)
doctor.vfsNotFull: Unit does not use --vfs-cache-mode full; many apps misbehave without it
doctor.notEnabled: %1 is not enabled; it will not mount at login (systemctl --user enable %1)
doctor.mountHung: Mounted at %1 but not responding — try: %2 restart
doctor.mountpointDirty: %1 is not empty while unmounted; rclone cannot mount over local files
doctor.notMountedActive: Service is active but nothing is mounted at %1
doctor.cacheFull: Cache is at %1 of %2 — rclone will evict, but uploads may stall
doctor.pending: %1 file(s) waiting to upload (keep the mount running)
doctor.diskLow: Only %1 free on the cache disk
doctor.notInPath: '%1' is not on your PATH yet (setup links it into ~/.local/bin)
remove.title: Remove %1 integration
remove.intro: This stops the mount and removes the service, bookmark, CLI link and (if you want) the rclone remote and local cache. Files on Google Drive are never touched.
remove.pendingRefuse: %1 file(s) are still waiting to be uploaded. Keep the mount running until they finish, or pass --force to drop them. (%2 status shows the count.)
remove.unitAdopted: %1 was written by you, not by omarchy-gdrive. Delete it anyway?
remove.remoteConfirm: Delete the rclone remote '%1' (your login token)? Your files stay on Google Drive.
remove.done: Done. Nothing of omarchy-gdrive is left on this machine.
gdrive.doctor.ownClient: Remote '%1' uses your own OAuth client_id
gdrive.doctor.sharedClient: Remote '%1' uses rclone's shared client_id, which Google retires during 2026. Fix: %2 setup --client
gdrive.why.title: Why you need your own Google client_id
gdrive.why.1: When rclone logs in to Google it identifies itself with a 'client_id'. By default every rclone user in the world shares the same one, so Google throttles it hard, and Google is retiring it during 2026: mounts that still use it will stop working.
gdrive.why.2: Creating your own takes about five minutes in the Google Cloud Console, is free, and gives you a private, much faster lane. The client_id is just an identifier; the client_secret is a password for your app and stays in ~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf (mode 600).
gdrive.why.3: Nothing is sent anywhere except to Google, and omarchy-gdrive never logs or prints these values.
gdrive.creds.nonInteractive: No credentials given and no terminal to ask; continuing with rclone's shared client.
gdrive.creds.optFile: I downloaded the client_secret_*.json from Google
gdrive.creds.optPaste: Paste client_id and client_secret by hand
gdrive.creds.optShared: Skip for now and use rclone's shared client (slow, dies in 2026)
gdrive.creds.howTo: Follow %1 then enter the path of the downloaded JSON file.
gdrive.creds.badPaste: That does not look like a Google client_id (…apps.googleusercontent.com) plus a secret.
gdrive.creds.sharedWarning: Using rclone's shared client_id. Expect throttling, and re-run 'omarchy-gdrive setup --client' before it is retired.
gdrive.creds.writeFailed: Could not write the client secret into %1
gdrive.creds.saved: Saved your OAuth client into remote '%1'
gdrive.creds.deleteJson: %1 still holds a copy of the client secret. rclone.conf has it now, so you can delete that file.
gdrive.creds.existingShared: Remote '%1' still relies on rclone's shared client_id.
gdrive.creds.upgradeNow: Switch to your own client_id now? (opens the browser once to log in again)
gdrive.creds.upgradeLater: Fine — do it any time with: %1 setup --client
gdrive.auth.title: Sign in to Google
gdrive.auth.1: Your browser will open on Google's consent screen. Pick the account whose Drive you want to mount.
gdrive.auth.2: If Google says the app is not verified, choose Advanced → Go to <your app> (unsafe). It is your own app; the warning is because you created it in test mode.
gdrive.auth.3: The token comes back to rclone on this machine only.
gdrive.auth.nonInteractive: A terminal is needed for the login. Run: rclone config reconnect %1:
gdrive.auth.failed: Google login did not complete. Run again: rclone config reconnect %1:
gdrive.auth.ok: Signed in — remote '%1' can list your Drive
gdrive.auth.verifyFailed: Signed in but listing '%1:' failed. Check the Drive API is enabled in your Google Cloud project.
setup.title: %1 setup
setup.unitUnparsed: Could not read remote and mount point from %1; using defaults.
setup.existingFound:
Found an existing service you created by hand:
  unit        %1
  remote      %2
  mount point %3
setup.optAdopt: Adopt it as is (recommended — nothing is changed or restarted)
setup.optReplace: Replace it with the omarchy-gdrive unit (restarts the mount)
setup.adopted: Adopted %1 — status/doctor/start/stop now manage it, the file stays yours.
setup.remoteExists: Remote '%1' already exists in rclone — reusing it.
setup.remoteWrongType: Remote '%1' is type %2, not %3. Pick another name with --remote.
setup.restartConfirm: Restart %1 now to apply? (unmounts for a few seconds)
setup.mountTimeout: %1 did not mount within 30 s. See: %2 logs
setup.bookmarkAdded: Added '%1' to the file manager sidebar
setup.doctorHint: Check it any time with: %1 doctor
doctor.tokenViaMount: Token valid — the mount is serving files
doctor.tokenThrottled: Google is throttling the shared client_id (rateLimitExceeded). The token is fine; this is exactly why you want your own: %1 setup --client
doctor.tokenUnreachable: Could not reach Drive to verify the token (offline or slow network); try again later
